zero_omission_notes.summary: Covers degrees of polynomials, geometric interpretation of zeroes as x-axis intercepts, and algebraic relationships between zeroes and coefficients of quadratic and cubic polynomials.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Zeroes of p(x) correspond to x-coordinates where y = p(x) cuts x-axis. A polynomial of degree n has at most n real zeroes.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Parabola Orientation
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: y = ax^2 + bx + c opens upwards if a > 0, downwards if a < 0.

detailed_sections.full_notes: For quadratic ax^2 + bx + c with zeroes α, β: α + β = -b/a and αβ = c/a.

practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.aim_or_objective: Find zeroes of x^2 + 7x + 10 and verify coefficient relations.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.conclusion_or_principle: Coefficients uniquely determine zero sum and product.

diagrams_figures_and_maps.structural_or_conceptual_explanation: Number of x-axis crossings equals number of real roots.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: Constructing quadratic polynomial from zeroes α and β.

textbook_exercises.question: Find zeroes of x^2 - 2x - 8 and verify relationship.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: The number of zeroes of y = p(x) intersecting x-axis at 3 distinct points is:
objective_questions_1_mark.explanation: Each x-axis intersection represents one real zero.

short_answer_questions.question: Find quadratic polynomial with sum -3 and product 2 of zeroes.

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: If α and β are zeroes of 2x^2 - 4x + 5, find α^2 + β^2.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: If zeroes of polynomial x^3 - 3x^2 + x + 1 are a-b, a, a+b, find a and b.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: A bridge arch is modeled as p(x) = -x^2 + 2x + 8.

qa.question: Find the zeroes of the arch path.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Writing sum of zeroes as b/a instead of -b/a.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: Always include the negative sign: α + β = -b/a.
